{{Short description|Complete cessation of oscillations in the theory of dynamical systems}}
In the theory of [[dynamical system]]s, '''amplitude death''' refers to a complete stop of [[oscillation]]s as a result of coupling interactions. The phenomenon can arise from systems either in [[periodic motion]] or [[chaos theory|chaotic motion]] before it goes to amplitude death.<ref>Renato E. Mirollo, [[Steven H. Strogatz]]: "Amplitude death in an array of limit-cycle oscillators" [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF01013676?LI=true]</ref> Understanding the complex behavior of oscillators is important for applications in pendulums, fluid, ecological, and population dynamics.

A dynamical system can go to amplitude death because of change in intrinsic parameters of the system or its interaction with other systems or its environment.<ref>V. Resmi, G. Ambika, R. E. Amritkar: "General mechanism for amplitude death in coupled systems" {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130223123622/http://pre.aps.org/abstract/PRE/v84/i4/e046212}}</ref><ref>V. Resmi, G. Ambika, R.E. Amritkar, G. Rangarajan: "Amplitude death in complex networks induced by environment"{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130224010651/http://pre.aps.org/abstract/PRE/v85/i4/e046211}}</ref>
Amplitude death can appear also because of the delay in the coupling between the systems<ref>Ramana Reddy, Sen A., Johnston, G. L.: "Time delay induced death in coupled limit cycle oscillators"[http://repository.ias.ac.in/85273/]</ref><ref>"Experimental evidence of time-delay-induced death in coupled limit-cycle oscillators": [http://repository.ias.ac.in/85277/]</ref>
